writeup: TIC 412843260 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.180865 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 2.17% dimming, while a secondary eclipse was not detected. The transit signal achieved a detection significance of 177.8 in the box-least-squares search, and pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal at a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 40.0, with the centroid offset 2.5 arcsec from the target position. The object does not appear in any of six variable-star catalogs checked. However, an open question remains: alternating eclipses in this candidate differ significantly in depth (odd/even z-score of 4.33), suggesting the true period may be twice the initially measured value. The corrected period of 4.180865 days accounts for this pattern, though the alternating eclipse depths warrant consideration in any future investigation of this system.
